summary.title: What is Serverless Computing?
summary.one_liner: Serverless computing hides server management from developers, who run code on pay-per-use cloud services (such as AWS Lambda) and manage no infrastructure themselves.
takeaways: Serverless does not mean there are no servers; the provider owns provisioning, scaling, patching and availability, so developers focus on code.
Pricing is usually metered per execution, so an idle serverless function costs nothing, unlike reserved servers.
Serverless services come as Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS) or Function-as-a-Service (FaaS); examples named include AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, Google Cloud Functions and IBM OpenWhisk.
Main limitations: less control over configuration and runtime options (e.g. JVM or OS settings), and not all applications, especially legacy systems, fit the model.
summary.summary: This Quora question thread collects many answers defining serverless computing as a cloud model where providers manage servers, scaling and infrastructure while developers deploy code or single-purpose services. Answers cover benefits (auto-scaling, pay-per-use, microservices, event-driven design), trade-offs (reduced configuration control, unsuitable for some legacy systems), and examples such as AWS Lambda, API Gateway, S3, Auth0, Azure Functions and Google Cloud Functions. Several answers are informal or repetitive, and some contain self-promotion, so the page is a loose collection of opinions rather than a structured guide.
